HasExtraCardText.rationale: presentation only: read solely by EnchantmentModel.DynamicExtraCardText (EnchantmentModel.cs:60-81) and the card-UI nodes; no game-state reader. Out of scope per the shared contract's 'presentation/animation' waiver.

CanEnchantCardType.maps_to: CorruptedEnchantment.can_enchant (enchantments.py:480-484) -- `card_type == CardType.ATTACK`, matching Corrupted.cs:15-18. Enchantment.can_enchant (enchantments.py:51-61) + the subclass override. Base CanEnchant (EnchantmentModel.cs:273-294) rejects CardType 4/5/6 (Status/Curse/Quest), then CanEnchantCardType, then an Unplayable card whose pile is PileType.Deck, then a card that already has a (non-stackable) enchantment. The sim folds CanEnchantCardType into each subclass's own can_enchant and replaces the pile-qualified Unplayable test with an unconditional `not card.is_playable` -- equal in practice because every ported grant enchants a DECK card (probe `grants`).

guards.what: BR-1 (blast radius, NOT a new mechanism): Hook.cs:1490-1499 applies the source card's Enchant*Additive then Enchant*Multiplicative to the running damage BEFORE either listener loop (Hook.cs:1314-1319 is the block twin); the sim registers the enchantment as an ordinary hook listener (combat.py:130-133) so its factor is pooled into the same sum/product as everyone else's (hooks.py:52-78, applied once at cmds.py:57-58)
guards.issue: ALREADY RECORDED, same verdict at every site (rule 3): audits/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard N3 names this explicitly ("This includes card-enchantment bonuses, which the sim registers as ordinary hooks (combat.py:133) rather than as C#'s explicit pre-step (Hook.cs:1490-1499)") and audits/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 13 clause (b) carries the block half. NOT re-verdicted here; recorded because THIS unit is in the blast radius, and with a sharper witness than either seam record states. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/enchantment_probes.py order`): a Corrupted Strike (base 6) with Strength 3 deals 13 in the sim and 12 in the game -- C# folds 6 * 1.5 = 9 and then adds Strength 3; the sim sums 6 + 3 = 9 and then multiplies by 1.5. The additive-only control in the same probe (Sharp +2 with Strength +3 = 11) MATCHES, which isolates the multiplicative phase as the cause. The seam records' own liveness evidence is the Shrink x Vulnerable float case; this witness needs no float at all -- it is a pure phase-order difference, and it should be folded into damage_pipeline N3 by that record's owner.

guards.what: FOUR-VERB COVERAGE (enchant / upgrade+downgrade / transform / copy) -- stated explicitly so the hole cannot reopen silently. Verb 3, TRANSFORM: CardCmd.Transform (CardCmd.cs:369-451) removes the original from its pile and adds a freshly-built replacement; it never touches Enchantment, and the destroyed original takes its enchantment with it
guards.maps_to: TRANSFORM verdict: FAITHFUL, both engines drop the enchantment. C#: CardCmd.Transform's loop takes `item.GetReplacement(rng)`, calls `item.Original.RemoveFromCurrentPile()` (CardCmd.cs:400) and adds the replacement (CardCmd.cs:437/440); the word Enchantment does not appear anywhere in the method, and neither AfterTransformedFrom nor AfterTransformedTo (CardModel.cs:1625-1631, both empty virtuals -- SovereignBlade is the only override in the source) moves it. So the enchantment dies with the original. SIM: run.transform_card (run.py:406-470) and CardCmd.transform_to_random (cmds.py:415-449) both build the replacement with `make_card(...)`, which carries no enchantment. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys,random;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.run import RunState;from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;r=RunState(rng=random.Random(0));c=make_card('strike');r.deck=[c];e=make_enchantment('corrupted');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);n=r.transform_card(c,into=make_card('bash'));print(n.id, n.enchantment)"` -> `bash None`, matching C#. The in-combat twin (CardCmd.transform_to_random on a Sharp'd Strike) also prints a replacement with `enchantment=None`. Same result for all 17 ids. COVERAGE TABLE for this unit -- (1) ENCHANT: the CanEnchantCardType hook entry plus the reachability guard above. (2) UPGRADE / DOWNGRADE: cannot bite here, and that is now executed rather than assumed: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.enchantments import ALL_ENCHANTMENTS, Enchantment;print(sorted(k for k,v in ALL_ENCHANTMENTS.items() if v.attach is not Enchantment.attach))"` -> `['goopy','souls','steady','tezcataras_ember']`. Only those four override attach() to mutate a static card property (exhausts / retain / cost / eternal), so only those four can be undone by the card rebuild that upgrade()/downgrade() performs. This unit is not one of them -- it works through the modify_* hooks, which are read live off the still-attached enchantment -- so upgrade and downgrade are no-ops for it. (3) TRANSFORM: this entry, faithful. (4) COPY: guard EG2, gap. All four verbs are now on the record; before this pass transform and copy were 0/17.

guards.what: EG2: card COPY drops the enchantment. C# CardModel.CreateClone (CardModel.cs:2168) -> MutableClone -> DeepCloneFields re-attaches the source card's enchantment onto the copy -- CardModel.cs:1204-1209 `(EnchantmentModel)Enchantment.ClonePreservingMutability()`, `Enchantment = null`, `EnchantInternal(clone, clone.Amount)` -- and does the same for the Affliction two lines down (1210-1215). CreateClone itself throws unless the card sits in a COMBAT pile (CardModel.cs:2170-2173), so every copy site is a combat-pile copy. The sim's copy sites rebuild the card from its class and carry only the upgrade level.
guards.issue: MECHANISM EG2, one verdict at every site (rule 3). FIVE ported sim copy sites drop the enchantment, each a `type(card)()` / `make_card(card.id)` rebuild plus a re-upgrade loop with no `card.enchantment` carry: cards/trash_heap_cards.py:18-24 `_clone` (Dual Wield, DualWield.cs:35), powers.py:827-830 (JugglingPower.cs:48), relics/music_box.py:46-48 (MusicBox.cs:78), cards/anger.py:36-38 (Anger.cs:27) and relics/burning_sticks.py:30-32 (BurningSticks.cs:49). All five map to a C# `CreateClone()` call, so all five are the same defect. The sim's OTHER copy paths are correct and are what makes this a bug rather than a design choice: relics/bing_bong.py:37 and events/reflections.py:52 use `copy.deepcopy` (the enchantment rides along), relics/paels_growth.py:39-46 re-attaches Clone by hand, and the per-combat deck copy (run.py:1136 `copy.deepcopy`) carries it too. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.cards.trash_heap_cards import _clone;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;c=make_card('strike');e=make_enchantment('corrupted');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);print(type(c.enchantment).__name__, _clone(c).enchantment)"` -> `CorruptedEnchantment None`. The same one-liner run over all 17 ids prints `None` for every one of the 16 that any probe card accepts (souls needs an Exhaust card, so it was run against fiend_fire). RULE 6, both legs -- reachability of the copy site for THIS unit: ATTACK-only (Corrupted.cs:15-18), so cards/trash_heap_cards.py:18-24 `_clone` (Dual Wield, hand ATTACK|POWER -- trash_heap_cards.py:143-149), powers.py:827-830 (Juggling, every 3rd ATTACK played), relics/music_box.py:46-48 (first ATTACK played each turn) and cards/anger.py:36-38 (Anger copies itself). Every one of the five sites is ported and reachable (Dual Wield from the ported Trash Heap event pool, events/trash_heap.py:17; Anger from the Ironclad common pool; Juggling from cards/juggling.py; Music Box and Burning Sticks are ported relics). LIVENESS: LIVE. The copy is an Attack: in the game it deals 1.5x and costs its owner 2 unblockable HP per play; in the sim it is a plain Strike. Grant path is the ported Symbiote event (events/symbiote.py:33-45). SECONDARY (false docstring): `_clone`'s docstring claims it "mirrors CreateClone for the sim's needs". It does not -- CreateClone carries the enchantment AND the affliction; `_clone` carries neither. Fifth entry in this stream's false-docstring list.
